title: Runtime error → quality-failure mapping and mitigation playbook
author: Maya Lin
content:
Summary

This playbook documents a compact, actionable mapping between observed serving/runtime errors and the likely downstream quality failures observed by evals, prompt-based probes, or customer telemetry. It is intended for oncall, regression engineers, and evaluation owners to quickly: (1) identify whether an operational/runtime anomaly is the root cause of a quality regression, (2) collect deterministic repro artifacts, and (3) apply the appropriate mitigation and rollback policy.

Scope

- Applies to Redwood production, dedicated, and private inference deployments.
- Covers common runtime error classes (OOM, kernel/fusion failures, quant mismatch, tokenization divergence, timeout/latency spikes, stale KV cache, nondeterministic seeds) and their mapped quality symptoms.
- Integrates with eval-harness probes, shadow runs, and the regression-triage escalation process.

Assumptions and prerequisites

- Access: oncall engineers have read access to telemetry dashboards and can trigger shadow runs using the eval-harness.
- Tooling: the runbook assumes the following services are available:
  - probe-fabricator (internal) for creating probe variants
  - shadow-orchestrator for mirrored traffic replay
  - eval-harness for deterministic replay and slice-level scoring
  - telemetry (Kibana/Tempo/Prometheus) preconfigured with the naming conventions below

Failure mapping table (quick reference)

| Runtime error class | Typical signals (telemetry / logs) | Likely quality symptoms | First-line actions | Triage owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OOM during decode | worker_crash_count↑, CUDA_OOM in logs, partial responses | Truncated or abruptly-ended completions, missing final tokens | Reproduce with smaller batch / sample; check model memory profile; fallback to lower-context or quant variant | runtime | 
| Kernel/launch failures (CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH) | launch_errors, kernel_retry_count↑, service restarts | Sporadic incorrect tokens, unexpected token repetition, sporadic 500s | Check GPU driver/kernel version, review kernel selection logs, pin safe kernel build | infra/runtime |
| Quantization mismatch (int8/4-bit mismatch) | quant_fallback_count, high coherence-delta on evals | Semantic drift, coherence loss, hallucination increase | Shadow-run on fp16 or alternative quant profile, revert quant profile for subset | model-onboarding |
| Tokenizer divergence | tokenization_errors, unknown_token_rate↑ | Tokenization breaks, broken prompts, malformed JSON outputs | Re-run tokenization check on seed inputs; check tokenizer version; pin tokenizer/vocab | eng-developer-experience |
| KV-cache corruption / stale cache | KV_cache_miss_ratio↑, cache_invalidation_errors | Context hallucination, stale facts, cross-request leakage | Flush KV cache per model instance; replay with warmed cache vs cold cache | serving-runtime |
| Latency timeout / tail spikes | p99_latency↑, incomplete_stream_count↑, queue_length↑ | Partial responses, truncated streaming, time-limited completions | Shift to degraded model with higher throughput or reduce batch window; enable streaming fallback | eng-sre |
| Nondeterministic RNG / seed variance | stochastic_delta_metrics↑, high eval variance | Response instability across seeds, evaluation noise | Run multiple seeds; fix RNG seeding in runtime; mark high-variance slices | applied-ml/evals |

Note: the table above is a quick guide. Use the Investigation checklist below for a deterministic workflow.

Investigation checklist (numbered playbook)

1. Confirm user-visible impact
   - Query eval-harness for the implicated slice: run a high-priority probe set (n=100 by default) against the failing model+deploy config.
   - Key command (example):

     # Replay a named probe slice into the ev-harness shadow runner\     python tools/eval_harness/replay.py --slice-id "billing-faq-longcontext-v2" --model-id "redwood-2b-quant" --replay-mode shadow --output results.json

   - If eval-harness shows a delta in coherence or hallucination > ties_to_threshold (default 6 percentage points), escalate to oncall.

2. Correlate to operational telemetry within the window
   - Timeline: use the incident window T0 = when alert fired +/- 30 minutes.
   - Suggested Kibana queries: 
     - Errors: service:(inference-runtime) AND message:(OOM OR CUDA_ERROR OR quant) | timeslice:1m
     - Latency: metric:p99_latency{model="redwood-*"} | group_by:model,region | compare_to:baseline(24h)

3. Perform deterministic replay and A/B compare
   - Reproduce on a single worker instance:
     - Capture the original request payload and seed (if present). Save as request_seed.json.
     - Use eval-harness deterministic-run to replay with identical RNG/kv-state flags:

       python tools/eval_harness/deterministic_run.py --input request_seed.json --model redwood-2b-quant --seed 42 --kv-warm False --output replayed.json

   - Compare tokens with diff tooling (tok-diff --gold gold.json --candidate replayed.json). If token-level divergence exists but runtime had no error logs, suspect tokenizer drift or model weight mismatch.

4. Isolate across variants
   - Run the same seed against:
     a) fp16 baseline (redwood-2b-fp16)
     b) alternate quant profile (redwood-2b-q4f16-safe)
     c) different runtime kernel build (kernel-v2 vs kernel-v1)
   - Record the slice-level metrics (coherence, factuality, BLEU-like for structured outputs). Use the provided CSV schema (see below) to standardize reports.

CSV report schema (example header line)

model_variant, kernel_build, seed, kv_warm, latency_ms, p_token_match, coherence_score, hallucination_rate, run_id
redwood-2b-quant,kernel-v2,42,False,180,0.87,0.72,0.09,run-2026-02-18-01

5. Decision matrix and mitigations

- If the problem reproduces only on quantized variants and not on fp16:
  - Immediate action: route traffic away from quantized pool for the affected model (traffic-split 0.2 fallback to fp16).
  - Medium-term: mark quant profile as suspect and create a quantization-tuning ticket with the model-onboarding team.

- If kernel launch errors correlate with a driver or kernel upgrade in the same window:
  - Immediate action: roll kernel to the previous stable build (kernel-v1) using staged rollout: 10%→30%→100% if health metrics pass.

- If OOMs occur under increased tail latency and queue depth:
  - Immediate action: reduce batch_size and enable micro-batching for the model route. If not feasible, enable dedicated fallback nodes with larger GPU memory.

- If tokenizer divergence is the root cause:
  - Immediate action: pin tokenizer version used by the producer of the prompt (client-side or SDK). Re-run the prompt normalization job across recent traffic to identify impacted customers.

Rollback and rollout policy (short)

- Fast rollback: use the service rollback API to return the deployment to the last green commit. Target RTO: < 20 minutes for critical customer-impacting regressions.
- Canary rollout: for any change that touches quant profiles, runtime kernels, or tokenizer versions, use the following canary policy: 1% (30m) → 10% (1h) → 50% (2h) → 100% (monitoring pass). Abort criteria: quality delta > 3 percentage points on top 3 priority slices OR p99 latency deviation > 25%.

Telemetry and metrics to collect (for postmortem and causal attribution)

- System metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, queue_length, CPU/GPU_util, host_oom_count, kernel_launch_errors.
- Model metrics: per-slice coherence_score, hallucination_rate, token_match_rate, kv_cache_miss_ratio.
- Logs: worker stderr/stdout for the incident window, kernel selection logs (/var/log/redwood/kernel_selector.log), quant-pipeline debug logs.
- Artifacts: request_seed.json, replayed.json, gold.json, CSV report (per CSV schema), kernel_build_id, model_artifact_hash.

Escalation matrix and ownership

- 1st responder (oncall runtime): confirm reproducibility and perform emergency mitigations (traffic routing, micro-batching, flush KV).
- 2nd responder (model-onboarding + applied-ml): run eval-harness A/B tests, inspect quant artifacts, validate fidelity against gold prompts.
- 3rd responder (infra/SRE): investigate kernel/driver/host-level failures and perform rollbacks.
- Product/Customer Success: notified for any customer-facing degradation > 10% of requests or any SLA breach.

Example incident timeline (fictional)

- T0 (09:12): Customer reports malformed JSON responses for billing assistant. Alert fires: eval-sentinel slice "billing-faq-longcontext" coherence_drop = 12ppt.
- T0+6m: Oncall sees CUDA_OOM spikes for redwood-2b-quant across two hosts.
- T0+12m: Deterministic replay reproduces truncation on quant variant but not on fp16. Traffic routed 100% to fp16 fallback.
- T0+90m: Model-onboarding team begins quant-profile investigation; identify new quant pack introduced earlier that day. Postmortem: quant pack regression — follow quant rollback process.

Operational checklists (copyable)

- Minimum reproduction artifact checklist:
  1. request_seed.json (full request + seed)
  2. model_artifact_hash.txt
  3. kernel_build_id.txt
  4. logs.tar.gz for T0±30m
  5. eval-harness result CSV

- Quick commands
  - Fetch last 1 hour OOM logs (Kibana API):
    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KIBANA_TOKEN" \"https://kibana.internal/api/logs/search?q=CUDA_OOM&from=now-1h\" > ooms.json

  - Deterministic replay (example):
    python tools/eval_harness/deterministic_run.py --input request_seed.json --model redwood-2b-quant --seed 42 --kv-warm False --output replayed.json

Post-incident follow-ups

- Short RCA (3 business days): owner_team must publish a short RCA summarizing: root cause, timeline, corrective actions, and test coverage added (link to PRs).
- Add a new eval probe(s) to cover the failing slice or failure mode (probe-fabricator ticket must include: representative prompts, expected outputs, and automated score thresholds).
- If quant or runtime kernel was root cause: add nightly regression job in eval-harness that runs the failing slice across candidate quant/kernel builds before promotion.

Related pages

- confluence://applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/throughput-fidelity-tradeoff-matrix-and-acceptance-protocol-2026
- confluence://applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-impact-synthesis-for-prompt-families-2026

Appendix: common Kibana/PromQL snippets

- P99 latency change (Prometheus):
  increase(p99_latency_seconds{service="inference-runtime",model=~"redwood-.*"}[1h]) > 0.25

- Kernel error count (Kibana query):
  service:"inference-runtime" AND message.keyword: "CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH" AND @timestamp:[now-60m TO now]

- Tokenizer divergence check (python):
  from tokenizers import Tokenizer
  t = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer-v3.json')
  print(t.encode('```Customer prompt snippet```').tokens)

Document maintenance

- Owner: engineering (applied-ml + serving-runtime rotation). Review cadence: quarterly or after any critical regression.
- Change log: keep a short changelog at the top of this page for kernel/quant/tooling updates.

End of playbook.
